title: LLM call record
description:
One record per LLM request/response made by an agent. Written as a line of JSONL on the Minecraft VM (source of truth), then shipped to Elasticsearch by Filebeat (the view). Field names and types must stay in sync with infra/elk/index-template.json -- that mapping is 'dynamic': 'strict', so an unexpected field is a hard indexing error rather than a silent surprise. That is deliberate.

NOTE ON 'bot' vs 'agent': the game agent is 'bot.*', NOT 'agent.*'. ECS permanently reserves 'agent.*' to describe the SHIPPING agent, and Filebeat injects agent.name/type/version into every event. Using agent.* here collides with that and silently rejects every document. Do not rename it back.

run_id.description: Identifies one continuous experiment. Lets you compare soak runs and, critically, filter a bad run out of analysis without deleting it.

name.description: Stable per-agent id, e.g. 'scout-01'. Under 'bot' not 'agent' -- see the ECS collision note above.

trigger.description: What caused this inference. Handoff doc S9.3 -- decisions are event-driven, never per-tick.

tick.description: Server tick. The join key for correlating against Paper logs in Kibana.

endpoint.description: Which Ollama host served this. Attribution matters once inference is split across the 5080 and the Mac Studio.

total_duration_ns.description: Ollama returns these five directly. load_duration_ns is the one to watch -- a nonzero value means the model was evicted and reloaded, which is the usual cause of surprise latency when agents share a GPU.

schema_valid.description: Did the structured output actually parse against the tool-call schema? The single most useful column here -- it turns 'the model is flaky' into a measurable rate.

system_hash.description: sha256 of the system prompt. System prompts repeat constantly; storing the hash plus one copy elsewhere keeps index size sane, and it makes 'which prompt version produced this behaviour' answerable.

text.description: Flattened prompt text, analysed for full-text search.

messages.description: Full verbatim request messages. Mapped 'flattened' in ES -- structurally queryable, exempt from field-count limits.

outcome.description: Filled in AFTER the decision is executed. This is what makes the corpus analysable rather than merely archived -- without it you cannot ask which decisions preceded a death or a stuck loop.
